title: Cessna Citation Longitude

sources.title: Cessna Citation Longitude / Garmin G5000 (public knowledge)

intro: The Cessna Citation Longitude is a business jet with two engines at the rear. Its cockpit has large screens, a control wheel for each pilot, and a short pedestal with the throttles. It can be flown by one pilot, so the layout is compact.

areas.name: Glareshield: autopilot and autothrottle
areas.text: The strip under the windscreen with the autopilot panel and the warning lights.

panels.name: Glareshield: autopilot and autothrottle
panels.text: This panel is the remote control of the autopilot and the autothrottle. The pilot sets the speed, heading, course and height and chooses the modes with buttons.
panels.context: The pilot uses it after take-off and on the approach. The autothrottle moves the engine power by itself.

controls.name: AP, YD and A/T buttons
controls.text: These buttons switch on the autopilot (AP), the yaw damper (YD) and the autothrottle (A/T). The yaw damper stops the tail from swinging.
controls.context: The pilot switches them on soon after take-off and keeps watching.

controls.name: HDG, NAV and APR buttons
controls.text: These buttons choose how the autopilot steers: HDG flies the set heading, NAV follows the planned route, APR follows the runway landing guidance.
controls.context: The pilot picks one at a time. The chosen mode is shown on the main screen.

controls.name: FLC, VS, ALT and VNAV buttons
controls.text: These buttons choose how the autopilot goes up and down: FLC holds a speed in a climb or descent, VS holds a climb rate, ALT holds the height and VNAV follows the planned height path.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to climb, level off and descend.

controls.name: Speed, HDG, CRS and ALT knobs
controls.text: These knobs set the targets for the autopilot: speed, direction, the course for radio navigation and height.
controls.context: The pilot dials in what the controller asks for.

controls.name: MASTER WARNING / CAUTION
controls.text: These lights come on when something needs the crew's attention. The red one is a warning and the amber one a caution. Pressing resets it.
controls.context: The pilot reads the message on the engine screen.

areas.name: Three large displays
areas.text: The big screens in the middle of the dashboard.

panels.name: Three large displays
panels.text: Large screens show the flying information and the map. They replace round dials. The gear handle sits beside them.
panels.context: The pilot looks at the screens while flying and uses the handle before landing.

controls.name: PFD (each pilot)
controls.text: This screen shows the horizon, speed, height and climb rate, with the autopilot modes at the top.
controls.context: PFD means primary flight display. Each pilot seat has one.

controls.name: MFD (centre)
controls.text: This screen in the middle shows the map, the engine information and diagrams of the aircraft's systems.
controls.context: MFD means multi-function display. The pilot changes pages with the touch screens on the pedestal.

controls.name: Standby instrument
controls.text: This small screen is the emergency instrument. It shows the horizon, speed and height by itself.
controls.context: If the main screens fail, the pilot flies with it.

controls.name: Landing gear handle

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The wheels fold into the aircraft.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The wheels are down and locked.

controls.text: This handle raises or lowers the wheels.
controls.context: The pilot raises the wheels after take-off and lowers them before landing.

areas.name: Pedestal
areas.text: The short block between the pilots with the touch screens, the throttles, the speed brake lever and the flap lever.

panels.name: Pedestal
panels.text: The pedestal holds the touch screens for the flight plan and the radios, the throttles, the speed brake lever and the flap lever.
panels.context: The pilot uses it throughout the flight. The throttles are moved by the autothrottle when it is on.

controls.name: Touchscreen controllers (GTC)
controls.text: These touch screens work like a tablet. The pilot taps them to enter the flight plan, tune the radios and change settings.
controls.context: GTC means Garmin touchscreen controller. They are the main way to enter data.

controls.name: Throttles with reversers
controls.text: These two levers set the engine power. The buttons on them disconnect the autothrottle, and the small levers reverse the push of the engines.
controls.context: The pilot pushes them forward for take-off and pulls them back to slow down for landing.

controls.name: Speed brake lever
controls.text: This lever opens the speed brakes, panels on the wings that slow the aircraft.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to descend or slow down quickly.

controls.name: Flap lever
controls.text: This lever sets the flaps, the parts of the wing that give more lift at low speed.
controls.context: The pilot sets a small amount for take-off and more for landing.

areas.name: Overhead panel
areas.text: The ceiling panel above the pilots with the system switches.

panels.name: Overhead panel
panels.text: This panel holds the switches for the electricity, fuel pumps, outside lights and ice protection.
panels.context: The pilot sets them up at the start and uses the ice protection in clouds.

controls.name: Electrical panel
controls.text: These switches control the batteries and the generators that supply electricity.
controls.context: The pilot switches the batteries on first and the generators once the engines run.

controls.name: Fuel panel
controls.text: These switches control the fuel pumps that feed the engines from the tanks.
controls.context: The pilot switches them on before the engine start.

controls.name: Exterior lights
controls.text: These switches turn on the lights outside the aircraft: beacon, position lights, strobes, landing and taxi lights.
controls.context: The pilot switches them on in steps from engine start to take-off.

controls.name: Anti-ice
controls.text: These switches heat the wing edges, the engine inlets and the windows to stop ice forming.
controls.context: The pilot uses them in clouds in cold air.

areas.name: Control wheel, throttles and pedals
areas.text: The controls for the pilot's hands and feet: the wheel, the throttles on the pedestal and the pedals.

panels.name: Control wheel
panels.text: Each pilot has a control column with a wheel. Thumb buttons on the wheel handle trim, autopilot and radio.
panels.context: The pilot flies with the wheel and uses its buttons without letting go.

controls.name: Control wheel
controls.text: Pushing the wheel forward lowers the nose and pulling it back raises it. Turning it rolls the aircraft left or right.
controls.context: The column moves the elevator at the tail and the wheel moves the ailerons on the wings.

controls.name: Pitch trim switch
controls.text: This thumb switch on the outer horn trims the nose. Pushing it up trims the nose down and pushing it down trims the nose up.
controls.context: Trim lets the aircraft fly steadily without constant force on the wheel.

controls.name: AP / trim disconnect
controls.text: Pressing this red button on the wheel switches off the autopilot and the yaw damper and stops the trim.
controls.context: The pilot presses it to take over the flying.

controls.name: Microphone switch
controls.text: Pressing this switch on the wheel horn makes the radio send while it is held.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to talk to the controller.

panels.name: Throttles and pedestal handles
panels.text: The levers the pilot's hand reaches on the pedestal: two throttles with their buttons, the speed brake and flap levers and the parking brake.
panels.context: The pilot uses them in every phase of the flight.

controls.name: Throttle 1
controls.text: This is the left throttle. It has stops for CUTOFF, IDLE, CRU, CLB and TO. Pushing it forward gives the left engine more power.
controls.context: The engines are run by a computer (FADEC), so each stop sets a power the computer manages.

controls.name: Throttle 2
controls.text: This is the right thrust lever. It works like the left one for the right engine.
controls.context: The pilot normally moves both together.

controls.name: TO/GA button
controls.text: Pressing this button on the outer side of the left throttle sets the flight director to the take-off or go-around mode.
controls.context: The pilot presses it at the start of the take-off or to go around.

controls.name: Speed brake lever
controls.text: Moving this lever back opens the speed brakes and forward closes them.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to slow down.

controls.name: Flap lever
controls.text: Moving this lever forward or back changes the flap setting by one step between 0, 15 and 35.
controls.context: The pilot sets a smaller setting for take-off and 35 for landing.

controls.name: Autothrottle disconnect buttons
controls.text: Pressing these buttons on the throttle grips switches the autothrottle off.
controls.context: The pilot takes over the engine power by hand.

controls.name: Thrust reverser levers
controls.text: These levers on the throttles send the engine push forward to slow the aircraft after landing.
controls.context: The pilot lifts them just after touchdown. The catalog notes that the standard aircraft does not have thrust reversers.

panels.name: Pedals, gear and parking brake
panels.text: The pedals on the floor and the two handles on the dashboard.
panels.context: These are used on the ground and for landing.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: Pushing a pedal turns the rudder, the vertical flap on the tail. The tops of the pedals are the toe brakes. The pedals also steer the front wheel a few degrees.
controls.context: The pilot stays straight on the runway with them.

controls.name: Parking brake handle
controls.text: Pulling this T-handle on the pilot's lower left panel sets the parking brake, with the toe brakes pressed. Pushing it releases the brake.
controls.context: The pilot sets it when the aircraft stands still.

controls.name: Landing gear handle
controls.text: Moving this wheel-shaped handle up folds the wheels away and moving it down lowers them.
controls.context: The pilot lowers it for landing and raises it after take-off.
